question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Tokyo, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

notes.anthropic: Converted 200-year-old bathhouse; since 1993 the key bridge between Japanese postwar masters (Kusama, Lee Ufan, Miyajima) and the international scene.
notes.openai: Landmark bathhouse gallery with exceptional postwar and contemporary Japanese artists, international fairs and deep institutional reach.

notes.anthropic: Global-facing programme in photography and contemporary art, with Maebashi/NY/LA history and a heavy fair presence; anchor of the complex665 building.
notes.openai: Central to Japanese contemporary art since the 1990s, with a formidable roster spanning conceptual art, painting and photography.

notes.anthropic: Yayoi Kusama's long-time Tokyo dealer, with Singapore and Shanghai outposts and a strong pan-Asian conceptual roster.
notes.openai: Internationally influential gallery closely associated with Yayoi Kusama and major artists from Japan and Southeast Asia.

notes.anthropic: Rigorous programme of Japanese artists (Yasumasa Morimura, Tomoko Yoneda, Shimabuku) with consistent museum placements.
notes.openai: Museum-caliber programme led by major Japanese artists including Masato Kobayashi, Shigeo Toya and Yukio Fujimoto.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1996; helped launch Nara, Murakami and Kusama internationally and remains one of Tokyo's most fair-active dealers.
notes.openai: Pivotal in establishing the global reputations of Yoshitomo Nara, Takashi Murakami and a generation of Japanese painters.

notes.anthropic: Since 1994 the platform for Aida Makoto, Yamaguchi Akira and 'Neo-Nihonga'; strong Asian network with Singapore and Beijing ties.
notes.openai: Long-running international gallery known for politically and socially engaged art from Japan and across Asia.

notes.anthropic: Tokyo branch of the French mega-gallery; high-profile shows of Murakami, JR, Sophie Calle and Japanese debuts of blue-chip names.
notes.openai: Tokyo branch of the influential global gallery, presenting internationally prominent artists alongside Japanese figures.

notes.anthropic: Pace's permanent Tokyo space (2024) in Azabudai Hills, bringing international blue-chip programming to central Tokyo.
notes.openai: Major global gallery whose substantial Azabudai space brings blue-chip contemporary and postwar programmes to Tokyo.

notes.anthropic: Critically respected programme linking Mono-ha and Gutai legacies to younger international artists; regular at Art Basel and Frieze.
notes.openai: Critically respected programme of conceptually rigorous artists, with strong biennial, institutional and international-fair visibility.

notes.anthropic: Takashi Murakami's gallery arm, incubator for a generation of younger Japanese artists and a global-facing brand.
notes.openai: Takashi Murakami's influential gallery platform for Japanese and international artists linked to contemporary visual culture.

notes.anthropic: Defined the pop/illustration-to-fine-art crossover (Hajime Sorayama, Keiichi Tanaami, Haroshi); multiple Tokyo venues and heavy fair presence.
notes.openai: Globally visible platform connecting contemporary art with underground culture, illustration, design and popular media.

notes.anthropic: Elegant Ginza mainstay showing Sugimoto, Rinko Kawauchi, Olafur Eliasson and other international names since 1995.
notes.openai: Prestigious Ginza gallery representing major conceptual and photographic artists, including Hiroshi Sugimoto and Sophie Calle.

notes.anthropic: Small but internationally influential; a fixture of Basel/Liste-type discourse and a model for artist-led curatorial exchange.
notes.openai: Internationally connected gallery whose adventurous programme has introduced important Japanese and overseas artists.

notes.anthropic: Sharp younger-generation programme; consistent presence at Art Basel Hong Kong and Frieze.
notes.openai: Highly regarded younger gallery supporting rigorous emerging and mid-career artists with growing institutional recognition.

notes.anthropic: Large-scale space formed by the merger of three veteran dealers; ambitious shows of Chim↑Pom, Ei Arakawa and others.
notes.openai: Ambitious large-scale gallery formed from three respected predecessors, with an established roster of leading Japanese artists.

notes.anthropic: Conceptually driven programme (Ryan Gander, Simon Fujiwara, Koki Tanaka) with strong European connections.
notes.openai: A key gallery for conceptual, minimalist and post-conceptual art, with a distinguished roster and sustained critical standing.

notes.anthropic: Museum-quality installations by Mika Ninagawa, Yuko Mohri and Sanya Kantarovsky; a driver of Tennozu's rise.
notes.openai: Fast-rising gallery with a strong generation of Japanese artists and regular participation in major international fairs.

notes.anthropic: Japan's first contemporary gallery (1950); historic for Mono-ha and for opening Beijing's 798 with BTAP.
notes.openai: Founded in 1950, this historically crucial gallery fostered Japanese avant-garde art and early exchange with China and Korea.

notes.anthropic: Fast-rising gallery with Tennozu and Roppongi spaces, mixing international emerging names with Japanese mid-career artists.
notes.openai: Expanding contemporary programme pairing prominent international names with established and emerging Japanese artists.

notes.anthropic: Thoughtful programme (Yuki Onodera, Kenji Yanobe collaborations, international photography) with growing fair visibility.
notes.openai: Internationally oriented gallery recognized for carefully developed exhibitions by emerging and established artists.

notes.anthropic: Multiple Tokyo spaces bringing internationally trending painters to Japan and supporting Japanese artists abroad.
notes.openai: Prominent multi-space gallery with an increasingly international roster and substantial presence at Asian and global fairs.

notes.anthropic: Corporate gallery operating since 1919 — Japan's oldest continuously running exhibition space, with a genuinely experimental free programme.
notes.openai: One of Japan's oldest active art spaces, supporting experimental contemporary exhibitions through a major cultural programme.

notes.anthropic: New York gallery's Tokyo space; scholarly presentations of Gutai and postwar Japanese avant-garde alongside Western artists.
notes.openai: Scholarly international gallery especially important for postwar Japanese avant-gardes and cross-Pacific art histories.

notes.anthropic: Curatorially austere space run by Naoya Aoyama; a critics' favourite for conceptual and post-Mono-ha positions.
notes.openai: Small but critically influential gallery associated with conceptually precise artists and Tokyo's independent scene.

notes.anthropic: Large commercial operation with Hong Kong, Taipei, Singapore and Seoul branches; major secondary market in Gutai and postwar Japan.
notes.openai: Large, long-established dealer with particular strength in Gutai, postwar Japanese art and an expanding Asian network.

notes.anthropic: Politically engaged gallery, home of Chim↑Pom-era activism and post-3.11 art; punches far above its size critically.
notes.openai: Artist-focused gallery noted for experimental Japanese practices and strong relationships with curators and public institutions.

notes.anthropic: Influential young gallery in the Komagome cluster, exporting emerging Japanese painters to Liste and Art Basel.
notes.openai: Critically respected gallery representing an influential group of younger Japanese conceptual and multimedia artists.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run space that became a node in the international young-gallery network; launched many careers now shown worldwide.
notes.openai: Internationally recognized artist-run initiative whose collaborative programme has helped reshape Tokyo's younger gallery ecology.

notes.anthropic: Custodian of key postwar photography and conceptual estates (Kishin Shinoyama, Ei-Q) plus contemporary artists.
notes.openai: Research-oriented gallery especially important for reassessing Japanese conceptual, photographic and postwar practices.

notes.anthropic: Young gallery with an incisive eye for emerging artists and a growing presence at Asian fairs.
notes.openai: Independent gallery with a strong record of nurturing emerging artists and placing their work in institutional exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Curatorially ambitious Ginza Six gallery pairing international contemporary names with Japanese historical material.
notes.openai: Curatorially driven Ginza gallery presenting historically important postwar and contemporary artists in an international context.

notes.anthropic: Design-conscious space that made Bakurocho a destination; agile programme of emerging Japanese and overseas artists.
notes.openai: Distinctive contemporary space in a former parking structure, with a cross-disciplinary and internationally connected programme.

notes.anthropic: Lean, artist-focused programme of contemporary painting and sculpture; a regular at Liste and Asian fairs.
notes.openai: Respected project-based gallery supporting emerging and mid-career artists through closely curated exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Curator-run gallery with a quiet, research-based programme and consistent international fair participation.
notes.openai: Focused programme of intellectually rigorous Japanese artists, many with growing museum and biennial attention.

notes.anthropic: Two-venue gallery supporting figurative painting and sculpture by emerging and mid-career Japanese artists since 2004.
notes.openai: Established contemporary gallery with a consistent Japanese and international programme and long-standing fair participation.

notes.anthropic: Shinjuku gallery known for queer, performance and body-based practices, including Genesis P-Orridge and Tetsumi Kudo-adjacent lineages.
notes.openai: Critically minded gallery presenting distinctive emerging and established artists in an intimate Shinjuku setting.

notes.anthropic: City-funded institution (formerly Tokyo Wonder Site) whose exhibitions and residencies have launched many careers.
notes.openai: Tokyo Metropolitan Government platform supporting experimental exhibitions, residencies and emerging artists with international exchange.

notes.anthropic: Musashino Art University's free experimental space; annual guest-curated series are closely watched by critics.
notes.openai: Curator-led public gallery supported by Musashino Art University, known for experimental series and early-career commissions.

notes.anthropic: Photography and new-media focused; active in international exchange and prize-winning young artists.
notes.openai: Strong contemporary and photographic programme emphasizing conceptually engaged artists and international dialogue.

notes.anthropic: Scholarly programme rediscovering Japanese photography and outsider/queer histories (Toshio Matsumoto, Nobuyoshi Araki archives).
notes.openai: Historically informed gallery with particular strength in Japanese photography, performance documentation and experimental postwar art.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1970s; organiser behind the Echigo-Tsumari and Setouchi triennales, uniquely influential on Japan's art-festival model.
notes.openai: Long-established Daikanyama gallery linked to major public-art commissions, regional art projects and Japanese contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Free corporate kunsthalle with an internationally respected curatorial programme in Renzo Piano's glass-block tower.
notes.openai: Architecturally notable foundation space with a sustained record of commissioned and curatorially ambitious contemporary exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run space with an international exchange model; a key node for Tokyo's youngest experimental scene.
notes.openai: Artist-run space with an outsized international reputation for collaborative, irreverent and generation-defining exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Specialist in Japanese and Chinese photography with a serious publishing arm; key to the international photobook scene.
notes.openai: Internationally influential specialist in Asian photography, supported by an active and respected publishing programme.

notes.anthropic: Photo Gallery International, founded 1979 — Japan's pioneering fine-art photography dealer and print workshop.
notes.openai: One of Tokyo's most important photography galleries, with major Japanese estates and a strong international programme.
Permanent Tokyo outpost of one of the world's most powerful galleries, with exhibitions by internationally canonical artists.

notes.anthropic: Longest-standing international mega-gallery outpost in Tokyo, presenting museum-grade shows of its global roster.
Publisher-gallerist central to Daido Moriyama and Nobuyoshi Araki's global market; multiple Ginza spaces.
notes.openai: Leading photography gallery and publisher associated with important Japanese photographers and meticulously produced editions.

notes.anthropic: The LA gallery's Tokyo space; historically decisive for Superflat and for reintroducing postwar Japanese art to the West.

notes.openai: A leading Tokyo gallery for European and Japanese conceptual practices, distinguished by longevity and scholarly exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Three-floor Jingumae space presenting a young, cross-genre roster with strong exhibition design.
notes.openai: Emerging-artist gallery noted for polished exhibitions across painting, sculpture, installation and new media.

notes.anthropic: Photography-centred gallery in the Bakurocho cluster, active in international photo fairs.
notes.openai: Well-regarded gallery supporting emerging Japanese and international artists through concise, carefully installed exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Compact Jingumae gallery with a sharp eye for young painters and illustration-adjacent practices.
notes.openai: Visible platform for younger contemporary art at the intersection of painting, street culture and design.

notes.anthropic: Three-storey space combining contemporary shows with postwar Japanese art scholarship and publishing.
notes.openai: Spacious Kagurazaka-area gallery mounting ambitious exhibitions of modern, postwar and contemporary Japanese art.

notes.anthropic: Small Kagurazaka gallery with a socially and politically engaged programme and strong Asian exchange.
notes.openai: Independent gallery with an eclectic, socially attentive programme spanning emerging practices and historical rediscoveries.
Tokyo branch of the influential Los Angeles gallery long involved in exchanges between Japanese and American contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Curator-run experimental venue and residency-linked platform for the post-2020 generation of Tokyo artists.
notes.openai: Independent curatorial space in a former ryotei, hosting experimental exhibitions, research and international collaborations.
Independent gallery with a long record of presenting critically ambitious Japanese and international contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Artist-run centre, cafe and archive in Kichijoji; a long-running incubator for Tokyo's alternative scene.
notes.openai: Essential artist-led centre for emerging practices, performances, talks and community-building in western Tokyo.

notes.anthropic: Pioneering micro-residency and gallery, connecting Tokyo to international residency networks for over two decades.
notes.openai: Long-running residency and exhibition space fostering sustained exchange between Tokyo artists and international visitors.

notes.anthropic: Handles the Nobuo Sekine and On Kawara-adjacent legacies and politically engaged international artists; strong institutional ties.
Fumihiko Maki-designed cultural complex whose atrium and gallery have hosted landmark art and design shows since 1985.
notes.openai: Prominent public exhibition space where contemporary art, design, craft and performance reach a broad Tokyo audience.

notes.anthropic: Nagoya-rooted gallery whose Tokyo space shows rigorous abstraction and European conceptualists; long track record.

notes.openai: Major non-collecting exhibition venue presenting substantial surveys, commissions and thematic contemporary-art exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Free foundation space showing Fondation Louis Vuitton collection works and commissions in Omotesando.
notes.openai: Foundation-run exhibition space bringing major international artists and collection projects to a prominent Omotesando location.

notes.anthropic: West Tokyo gallery with a distinctive, criticism-driven programme for the youngest generation.
notes.openai: Independent gallery closely associated with experimental, internet-aware and politically alert younger Japanese practices.

notes.anthropic: Corporate cultural hall known for photography exhibitions and cross-disciplinary programming.
notes.openai: Corporate cultural venue best known for polished photography and contemporary-art exhibitions with international reach.

notes.anthropic: Successor to ARATANIURANO; conceptual and media-art programme with long-standing critical credibility.
Curator-founded gallery known for conceptual and socially engaged Japanese artists and off-site projects.
notes.openai: Established gallery presenting socially engaged installation, performance, media art and contemporary Japanese visual culture.

notes.anthropic: Contemporary photography specialist that helped define the post-2000 Japanese photo scene.
notes.openai: Influential platform for contemporary photography that has supported new Japanese image-makers, publications and curatorial projects.

notes.anthropic: Photography-leaning contemporary programme; among the first movers into the Tennozu art district.
Photography gallery with a distinctive editorial sensibility and a steady stream of first solo shows.
notes.openai: Respected specialist gallery for contemporary photography, known for sustained artist development and thoughtful exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Kansai-founded gallery with a long record in conceptual and sculptural practices, now anchored in Tokyo.
Contemporary arm of the venerable Galerie Nichido; consistent programme of mid-career Japanese and Asian artists.
notes.openai: One of Japan's longest-established commercial galleries, influential in modern yōga and continuing contemporary painting programmes.

notes.anthropic: Small Nakameguro gallery with a considered programme of emerging painters and sculptors.
notes.openai: Independent space recognized for understated, critically rigorous exhibitions by younger Japanese artists.

notes.anthropic: Harajuku venue bridging street/pop culture and contemporary art with frequent international collaborations.
notes.openai: Independent Harajuku complex mounting high-profile exhibitions across contemporary art, photography, fashion and design.

notes.anthropic: Curator-run gallery known for research-led solo presentations and support of experimental younger practices.
notes.openai: Curatorially focused gallery pairing contemporary practice with research into postwar Japanese art and visual culture.

notes.anthropic: Long-running space at the intersection of art, music and street culture, with strong international guest shows.
notes.openai: Cross-disciplinary gallery connecting contemporary art with influential graphic-design, music and fashion communities.
Young gallery gaining attention for experimental exhibitions and close engagement with Tokyo's emerging artist community.

notes.anthropic: Revived 1950s avant-garde building run by the Chim↑Pom circle; a hub for performance and countercultural programming.
Long-running dealer of drawing, print and conceptual work with an idiosyncratic international roster.
notes.openai: Independent gallery with a durable programme of Japanese and European artists and a strong emphasis on painting and sculpture.
Internationally oriented gallery with a programme spanning contemporary art, design and historically informed presentations.
Veteran contemporary dealer and project platform with longstanding connections across Japan's international art scene.

notes.anthropic: Curatorial nonprofit running residencies, the MAD education programme and exhibitions since 2001.

notes.openai: Emerging gallery presenting multicultural and interdisciplinary practices, often by artists working between Japan and abroad.
Focused gallery building dialogue between Japanese and Chinese contemporary artists through restrained, research-led exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: DNP's graphic-design gallery since 1986; internationally the most important venue for Japanese design exhibitions.
Free corporate space in Ginza with a well-regarded programme of emerging and mid-career Japanese artists.
Descendant of the legendary 1990s Roentgen Kunst Institut that first showed Murakami and Nara.
Veteran dealer in minimal and conceptual art, publishing editions with Japanese and European artists since the 1980s.
Long-established gallery showing painting and sculpture by mid-career Japanese artists.

notes.openai: Architecturally ambitious Omotesando venue presenting curator-led exhibitions on art, ecology, architecture and social change.

notes.anthropic: Quiet, conceptually focused gallery respected for tightly argued solo exhibitions.
Kyobashi gallery of long standing with a serious abstraction and print programme plus an annex for younger artists.
notes.openai: Long-running gallery respected for serious presentations of Japanese painting, sculpture, printmaking and installation.

notes.anthropic: Gallery pairing contemporary art with Japanese antiquities and craft, with an international collector base.
notes.openai: Internationally active gallery advancing sculptural and craft-rooted Japanese artists through major fairs and institutional placements.

notes.anthropic: Programme spanning contemporary art, craft and design culture; influential among younger collectors.
Gallery arm of Japan's leading art magazine; accessible programming that reaches a wide public audience.
notes.openai: Physical exhibition arm of a major Japanese art-media platform, providing visibility and sales support to contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Operating since 1974 with an annex space; a durable supporter of contemporary Japanese painting.
notes.openai: Veteran Kyobashi gallery with decades of commitment to idiosyncratic Japanese contemporary artists.
Established Harajuku gallery influential in street-derived, illustrative and pop-oriented contemporary art.
Highly visible Miyashita Park gallery presenting contemporary artists connected to painting, music, fashion and youth culture.
Prominent cultural-retail gallery hosting contemporary art, photography, publishing and popular-culture collaborations.

notes.anthropic: Founded 1964; brought Hockney, Kitaj and British art to Japan and represents senior Japanese painters.
Historic Ginza gallery (est. 1966) central to Japanese printmaking and to Yoko Ono/Fluxus-era exhibitions.

notes.openai: Exhibition space within Tokyo's key specialist art bookstore, important for artist publications and experimental projects.
Independent multi-level gallery presenting emerging and mid-career artists in painting, installation and interdisciplinary media.

notes.anthropic: Known for launching young Japanese artists via its Odyssey competition and for consistent fair participation.

notes.openai: Street-facing, always-visible project space whose compact installations extend contemporary art into everyday urban space.

notes.anthropic: Tokyo–New York gallery promoting Japanese artists internationally with a contemporary-meets-tradition programme.

notes.openai: Tennozu gallery with a globally oriented emerging programme and growing participation in Asian art fairs.
Cross-border gallery connecting Japanese contemporary artists with collectors and institutions across Greater China and Asia.

notes.anthropic: Kyoto house founded 1937; its Tokyo space stages scholarly shows linking classical Japanese art with contemporary practice.

notes.openai: Established gallery, also known as TSCA, supporting conceptually focused Japanese artists and international exchange.
Permanent Tokyo branch of the Osaka gallery, presenting contemporary Japanese art with particular attention to material traditions.

notes.anthropic: Japanese–Brazilian gallery bringing Latin American and diaspora practices into the Tokyo conversation.
Fluxus and multiples specialist since 1981; an archive-like resource for conceptual editions and artists' books.

notes.openai: Established contemporary gallery recognized for carefully sustained relationships with Japanese painters and sculptors.

notes.anthropic: Leading Japanese venue for art brut and outsider art, with strong international exhibition partnerships.

notes.openai: Independent gallery with an experimental programme spanning emerging art, performance, installation and collaborative projects.

notes.anthropic: Murakami-founded Nakano Broadway venue that turned otaku-adjacent subculture into a serious exhibition platform.
Warehouse project space anchoring the Komagome cluster; large-scale installations by emerging artists.
Compact Aoyama project space with a consistently experimental, non-commercial curatorial line.

notes.openai: Established gallery presenting Japanese postwar and contemporary work with a research-conscious, historically grounded approach.

notes.anthropic: Shared exhibition space of the Contemporary Art Dealers Association of Nippon; a rotating window on the whole gallery scene.

notes.openai: Scholarly gallery and publisher connecting contemporary work with modern architecture, prints, photography and Japanese avant-gardes.
Singular gallery known for uncompromising figurative, photographic and subcultural positions outside Tokyo's mainstream market.
Nakameguro gallery with a sustained international programme emphasizing materially expressive painting and sculpture.

notes.anthropic: East Tokyo gallery supporting mid-career and emerging artists, part of the Sumida/Ryogoku art cluster.

notes.openai: Influential photographer-run space supporting independent exhibitions, criticism and publishing outside the conventional commercial system.
